summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas states that sending salutations to anyone else is inappropriate, and the text breaks off in the middle of his exception.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence ('unless it be to one of the'). The Prophet is not named in the text; the heading is about salutations to Nabi.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that in a single sitting the Prophet recited a hundred times the istighfaar, 'O my Rabbi, forgive me and accept my repentance.'
Hudhayfah complains to the Prophet that his sharp tongue towards his family may lead him to Jahannam, and the Prophet tells him to seek forgiveness a hundred times daily.
notes: Two versions of the same incident are joined ('Another narration states...'). Not sure which Hudhayfah this is, so not matched to Hudhayfah bin Yamaan or Hudhayfah bin Mihsin.

summary: Anas says that on a journey the Prophet had them all seek forgiveness seventy times, and taught that Allaah forgives seven hundred sins of a servant who does so each day; the text breaks off mid-sentence.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence after 'during any day and'.

summary: Ali bin Rabee'ah relates that while he rode behind Ali he saw him ask Allaah for forgiveness and then smile, and that the Prophet had done the same and explained that Allaah laughs at a servant who knows none but Him forgives sins; the text breaks off.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence ('that none but He can'). Ali bin Rabee'ah is in the story as the rider who asked, so marked subject. OCR debris ('Mji -i iij') ignored.

summary: Abu Hurayrah says he has never seen anyone after the Prophet recite istighfaar more often than him; the quotation breaks off.
notes: Cut off mid-quotation. The Prophet is named only as the comparison, so marked mentioned.

summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah reports that a man with many sins came to the Prophet, who taught him a du'aa asking for forgiveness greater than his sins, and then told him Allaah had forgiven him.
notes: The man is unnamed and left out.

summary: Hannaad reports that Umar corrected a man who said only 'I seek forgiveness from Allaah and repent to Him', telling him to add the words asking Allaah to forgive him and accept his repentance.
notes: Hannaad is not in the approved list. He is a narrator of a later generation, so marked sahabi no.

summary: Sha'bi reports that Ali said he is surprised at someone who destroys himself when salvation is at hand, and that the salvation is istighfaar.
notes: The questioner is unnamed and left out.

summary: Abu Dardaa says there are glad tidings for the person who finds even a little istighfaar in his record of deeds.
Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that a person who recites a particular istighfaar three times will be forgiven even for fleeing from the battlefield.
Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that if people knew his sins not even two of them would walk behind him, and he would be glad if Allaah forgave even one of them.
notes: 'Abdullaah bin Rowtha' in the text is a nickname for Ibn Mas'ood, not a separate person, so not listed.

summary: Abu Hurayrah says that every day he seeks Allaah's forgiveness and repents twelve thousand times, in proportion to the debt he owes Allaah.

Abu Hurayrah is quoted in another version as saying the figure is in proportion to his sins, and Baraa bin Aazib explains that the verse 'do not throw yourselves into destruction' refers to one who sins and then despairs of Allaah's forgiveness, not to one who dies fighting.
notes: Two separate reports are joined: a variant of Abu Hurayrah's saying (see n03093), and Baraa's answer on Qur'aan 2:195 to an unnamed questioner (left out). Baraa identified by the kunya Abu Amaarah.

summary: Abu Dardaa relates that the Prophet described people whom Allaah will raise on the Day of Qiyaamah on thrones of pearls, neither prophets nor martyrs, who love one another for Allaah's pleasure and gather to remember Him.
notes: The Bedouin who asked is unnamed and left out.

summary: Amr bin Abasa reports the Prophet said there are people on the right of Ar-Rahmaan who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whose faces shine, who gather for Allaah's dhikr and choose the best words as one chooses the best dates.
Anas bin Maalik reports that the Prophet came upon Companions discussing their former ignorance and how Allaah guided them, and praised them, telling them to continue as they were.
notes: The Companions in the discussion are unnamed and left out.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says to speak often of Umar bin Khattaab, since speaking of him is speaking of justice and speaking of justice is speaking of Allaah.
Aa'isha says to adorn gatherings with sending salutations upon the Prophet and with speaking of Umar bin Khattaab.
Abdullaah bin Abbaas relates that when asked who the friends of Allaah are, the Prophet said they are the people whose sight reminds you of Allaah.
notes: The questioner is unnamed and left out.

summary: Handhala, a scribe of the Prophet, reports that he felt himself a hypocrite when his heart's state from the Prophet's gatherings faded at home with his family, and the Prophet told him that if he stayed as he was in his company the angels would shake hands with him, with a second version adding Abu Hurayrah's similar complaint.
notes: Two reports joined: Handhala's account with Abu Bakr, and a second narration from Abu Hurayrah. The text says 'Handhala Usayyidi'; matched to handhala-bin-rabee-tameemi on the basis that Usayyidi is a Tamim clan. Please check against the plain 'handhala' entry.

summary: Urwa bin Zubayr relates that when he proposed to Abdullaah bin Umar's daughter during Tawaaf, Ibn Umar stayed silent because they were remembering Allaah, and later in Madinah accepted the proposal and married him to her.
notes: The Prophet is named only as the mosque he was visited at, so marked mentioned. Abdullaah the son is identified only from 'his two sons Saalim and Abdullaah'. Sauda is the daughter, named in the text.

summary: Aa'isha relates that the Prophet said prayer after brushing the teeth with a miswaak is seventy times better than without it, and that silent dhikr is seventy times better than audible dhikr and will be rewarded by Allaah on the Day of Qiyaamah.
notes: Two separate sayings of the Prophet (miswaak with salaah, and silent dhikr) are joined under one narrator.

summary: Jaabir relates that at Baqee the Prophet asked for a body to be lifted from its grave and handed to him, and they found it was the man who used to raise his voice in dhikr.
notes: The dead man is unnamed and left out.

summary: Muhammad bin Ibraaheem Taymi relates the story of Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn, an orphan who after accepting Islaam was stripped of his uncle's goods, was told by the Prophet to stay at his door, and was buried at Tabook by Abu Bakr and Umar while the Prophet prayed for his pleasure.
notes: Two reports joined: Taymi's account (including Umar's remark), and Ibn Mas'ood's account of the burial at Tabook. The uncle and the mother are unnamed and left out.

summary: Uqba bin Aamir reports that the Prophet said of Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn that he is one who sighs deeply, because he remembered Allaah aloud through Qur'aan and du'aa.
Safiyya relates that the Prophet came to her while she was counting her tasbeehaat with four thousand date seeds and taught her to glorify Allaah as much as all of His creation.
notes: The text says only 'Safiyya'. Matched to safiyya-bint-huyay from the date-seed incident. Not safiyya-bint-abdul-muttalib, and not the unsure entry 'safiyya'. Please check.

summary: Another narration gives the dhikr as 'as much as everything He has created', and reports that Abu Safiyya, Abu Hurayrah and Sa'd counted their tasbeeh with stones or a knotted string.
notes: Several reports are joined: a variant wording of the dhikr, Yunus bin Ubayd's report from his mother about Abu Safiyya, Abu Hurayrah's string of knots, and an author's cross-reference to earlier narrations. Sa'd is not identified; the heading gives only 'Sa'd (RA)' and the Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas of n03110 is probably meant but is not stated here. His mother is unnamed and left out.

summary: Abu Nadhra relays an old man's account of being Abu Hurayrah's guest in Madinah, where he saw him count his tasbeeh with stones or date seeds while his slave woman refilled the bag for him, and was struck by his care for guests.
notes: Ends with 'The rest of the narration continues further.' The old man and the slave woman are unnamed and left out.

summary: Hakeem bin Daylami reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas used stones to count his tasbeeh.
notes: Hakeem bin Daylami is not in the approved list and is marked sahabi no as a narrator of the later generation.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar advises making dhikr only in a state of purity, and Abu Hurayrah relates that the Prophet said Allaah multiplies the reward of a good deed to a very great number, citing Qur'aan 4:40.
notes: Joins Ibn Umar's ruling, Abu Hurayrah's report, and a second narration from Abu Uthmaan. Abu Uthmaan Nahdi is not matched to the approved abu-uthmaan (?) entry, which may or may not be the same man.

summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal relates that the Prophet corrected several people's du'aas: he told one who asked for patience to ask for safety, explained that the perfect bounty is Jannah and rescue from Jahannam, and said that the du'aa of one who called on Dhul Jalaali wal Ikraam had been accepted.
notes: The people making du'aa are unnamed and left out.

summary: Anas bin Maalik relates that the Prophet visited a very weak man who had asked Allaah to bring his punishment forward, taught him the Qur'aanic du'aa for good in this world and the Hereafter, and the man was cured.
notes: The sick man is unnamed and left out.

summary: Basheer bin Khasaasiyah relates that the Prophet thanked Allaah for guiding him to Islaam, and that when Basheer asked him to pray that he die before him, the Prophet refused to make that du'aa for anyone.
notes: OCR debris at the end ('' '') ignored.

summary: Ubay bin Ka'b says the Prophet always began his du'aa for anyone with himself, and remarked that Moosa would have seen stranger things had he been more patient with his companion.
notes: Moosa's companion (Khidr, by the Qur'aan reference) is unnamed in the text and left out.

summary: Abu Ayyoob Ansaari reports that the Prophet always began his du'aa with himself, and Aa'isha told Ibn Abu Saa'ib, a lecturer in Madinah, not to contrive rhymed du'aas since the Prophet and Companions did not.
notes: Two reports joined: Abu Ayyoob's report and Aa'isha's advice. Ibn Abu Saa'ib is described as a lecturer in Madinah, so not matched to the approved abu-saaib (yes) entry.

summary: Umar corrects a man who prays for protection from trials by asking whether he wants his Lord to withhold family and wealth from him, and Muhaarib bin Dithaar reports his uncle's account of Ibn Mas'ood's pre-dawn du'aa for forgiveness, which Ibn Mas'ood linked to Ya'qoob's pre-dawn du'aa for his sons.
notes: Several reports joined: Umar's remark in two versions, and Muhaarib's account of his uncle hearing Ibn Mas'ood. The man and the uncle are unnamed and left out.

summary: Umar relates that whenever the Prophet made du'aa he raised his hands and passed them over his face on finishing.
Another narration says the Prophet would not lower his hands from a du'aa until he had passed them over his face on completing it.
notes: The narrator of 'another narration' is not named. OCR '(SPS-?)' in the text is taken to be the salutation.

summary: Umar says he saw the Prophet make du'aa at Ahjaaruz Zayt with his palms towards his face and pass them over his face afterwards, and Aa'isha says he raised his hands for so long in du'aa that she grew tired.
notes: Two reports joined: Umar's and Aa'isha's. Ahjaaruz Zayt is a place name.
